raw_record.question_text: How many little squares at least do we have to shade in the picture on the right in order that it have an axis of symmetry?

method.method_draft: Read the right-hand picture as a diamond-shaped grid with row lengths 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 7, 5, 3, 1. Label the cells by row from top to bottom and column from left to right within a centered 9-by-9 coordinate frame. Record the shaded cells. Since we may only add shaded squares and cannot change the outer grid, any possible final axis of symmetry must be one of the four symmetry axes of the diamond outline: vertical, horizontal, and the two diagonals through the center. For each candidate axis, reflect every currently shaded square; if its mirror cell is not shaded, that mirror cell must be added. Count the number of missing mirror partners for each axis. The diagonal running from upper right to lower left has only three missing mirror partners, while the other candidate axes require more. Therefore the minimum number of additional little squares to shade is 3.

最少需要补涂的是右上到左下对角轴对应的情况，因此至少要涂黑 3 个小正方形。
